definition_zh: 文明；文明社会；（某地某时期的）文化
definition_en: an advanced stage of human society with cities, writing and organised government, or the culture of a particular place and period
core_image: 河岸边升起的城墙、泥板文字与喧闹集市
scene: 博物馆的展柜里摆着泥板、青铜器和陶罐。Writing marked the birth of civilization in the river valley.
sceneCN: 这里 civilization 指「文明」（第 1 个义项：拥有城市、文字与制度的社会阶段）；句意是文字的出现标志着河谷文明的诞生。

senses.title: An advanced human society
senses.definition: a society with cities, writing, industry and organised government
senses.definitionCN: 拥有城市、文字、手工业与有组织政府的社会
senses.example: Ancient civilizations grew up along great rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 古代文明在大河沿岸发展起来。
senses.why: Farm surpluses freed people to build cities and keep written records, and that whole package became the mark of a civilization.
senses.whyCN: 农业剩余让人腾出手来建城市、留文字记录，这一整套就成了文明的标志。

senses.title: The stage of social development
senses.definition: the stage of social development that such societies have reached
senses.definitionCN: 这类社会所达到的社会发展阶段
senses.example: Trade and writing pushed the region towards civilization.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易与文字把这一地区推向了文明。
senses.why: The same noun also names the achieved stage, an abstract level rather than one single society.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也指达到的阶段，是抽象层次而不是某个具体社会。

senses.title: The culture of a place or period
senses.definition: the way of life, art and ideas of a particular place or period
senses.definitionCN: 某一地方或时期的生活方式、艺术与观念
senses.example: The gallery traces the civilization of the Silk Road.
senses.exampleCN: 这座美术馆梳理了丝路沿线的文化。
senses.why: Because a society and its culture were seen as one whole, the word widened to mean a whole way of life.
senses.whyCN: 社会与文化被看作一个整体，于是这个词扩展为整套生活方式。

intro.en: Civilization grows from the Latin word for a citizen, not from a word for bricks or walls.
intro.cn: civilization 出自拉丁语里表示公民的词，而不是砖瓦城墙一类词。

items.en: Civis meant a citizen of a town.
items.cn: civis 指城邦或城镇的公民。

items.en: Civilis described anything belonging to citizens.
items.cn: civilis 形容属于公民的事物。

items.en: Civiliser meant to make a place fit for citizens.
items.cn: civiliser 指让一个地方变得适合公民居住。

items.en: Civilization first named the process, then the result.
items.cn: civilization 先指这个过程，后指结果。

items.en: The word now also covers the culture of a region.
items.cn: 这个词如今也涵盖一个地区的文化。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the civil family, while the meaning group names large human groupings.
note.cn: 形近组列出 civil 这一家族，近义组列出各类人群共同体。

entries.definition: relating to citizens or to ordinary people rather than the army or the church
entries.definitionCN: 与公民或普通人有关的，而非军队或教会的

entries.definition: a person who is not a member of the armed forces
entries.definitionCN: 不属于武装部队的平民

entries.definition: to bring a society to a more developed way of life
entries.definitionCN: 把一个社会带向更发达的生活方式

entries.definition: people living together in an organised community
entries.definitionCN: 在有组织的共同体中共同生活的人们

entries.definition: the customs, art and beliefs of a group of people
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体的习俗、艺术与信仰

entries.definition: a group of people who live in the same area or share an interest
entries.definitionCN: 住在同一地区或共享某种利益的一群人

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the citizen root, the city skyline, the written record and the culture sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从公民词根、城市天际线、文字记录与文化义入手。

normal.en: Civilization hides civis, the Latin word for a citizen, so the word begins with people, not with buildings.
normal.cn: civilization 里藏着拉丁语 civis（公民），所以这个词的起点是人，不是建筑。

normal.en: A civilization needs four things: a city, a script, a law and a surplus of food.
normal.cn: 一个文明需要四样东西：城市、文字、法律和余粮。

normal.en: The -ization ending marks a process, so the word names both the journey and the settled result.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ization 表示过程，因此这个词既能指历程也能指结果。

normal.en: Civilized describes people, while civilization describes the whole society.
normal.cn: civilized 形容人，civilization 形容整个社会。

normal.en: A clash of civilizations is a phrase from politics, not from archaeology.
normal.cn: a clash of civilizations 是政治学说法，不是考古学说法。

abstract.en: Picture a mud-brick wall rising beside a river, with a scribe counting grain behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象河边的土砖城墙升起，墙后有书吏在清点粮食。

abstract.en: Picture a clay tablet pressed with wedge marks, the first receipt in history.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被压出楔形痕迹的泥板，那是历史上第一张收据。

abstract.en: Picture a museum case holding a pot, a coin and a broken tablet.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆展柜里放着一只陶罐、一枚硬币和一块残破的泥板。

examples.en: The museum shows how civilization began in river valleys.
examples.cn: 博物馆展示了文明如何在河谷中起步。

examples.en: Every civilization leaves behind its tools, its laws and its stories.
examples.cn: 每个文明都会留下自己的工具、法律与故事。

examples.en: Scholars study the civilization of the Silk Road through its art.
examples.cn: 学者通过艺术品研究丝路沿线的文化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 civil 想成「市民的」，ization 想成「化」：市民聚居成城，就有了文明。

root: 源自拉丁语 civis（公民）与 civilis（公民的），经法语 civiliser 进入英语，本义是让一个地方适合公民聚居。

sensesIntro.en: From citizens to cities, then to a stage of development, and finally to a whole culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 从公民到城市，再到发展阶段，最后扩展到整套文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled town with a scribe and a market inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：带城墙的城镇，里面有书吏和集市。

branches.en: Cities, writing and law turn a settlement into a civilization.
branches.cn: 城市、文字与法律把聚落变成文明。

branches.en: The noun also names the stage a society has reached.
branches.cn: 这个名词也指一个社会达到的阶段。

branches.en: A society and its culture share the same word.
branches.cn: 社会与其文化共用一个词。

branches.en: The society and its level of development take one noun.
branches.cn: 社会与其发展水平用的是同一个名词。

branches.en: The culture branch keeps the everyday life of that society.
branches.cn: 文化分支保留了该社会的日常生活。

intro.en: One verb base grows a noun, two adjectives and a set of related civil words.
intro.cn: 一个动词词基长出名词、两个形容词以及一组 civil 相关词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin civis, a citizen, so every member of the family points back to town life.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 civis（公民），因此这一家族的每个成员都指向城镇生活。

items.meaning: to bring a society to a developed stage
items.example: Traders helped civilize the river ports.
items.exampleCN: 商人帮助河港走向文明。

items.meaning: having an advanced society or good manners
items.example: The city had a civilized air.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有一种文明的气息。

items.example: The railway had a civilizing effect on the coast.
items.exampleCN: 铁路对沿海产生了开化作用。

items.meaning: the advanced society or its stage
items.example: Writing is a mark of civilization.
items.exampleCN: 文字是文明的一个标志。

items.example: Old civilizations traded along the sea.
Civil law grew beside religious law.
items.exampleCN: 民法与宗教法并行发展。

items.meaning: a person outside the armed forces
items.example: The bridge was open to civilians.

latinEntries.example: Civis gave English the whole civil family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: civis 给了英语整个 civil 家族。

latinEntries.example: Civilis passed through French into English.

definition_zh: 使文明；教化；使有教养
definition_en: to bring a society to a more developed way of life, or to make someone behave in a more polite and educated way
core_image: 荒地上同时立起学校、道路与法庭
scene: 老师带学生看老照片，照片里是从前的村路。Missionaries tried to civilize the remote islands.
sceneCN: 这里 civilize 指「使文明」（第 1 个义项：把一个社会带向更发达的生活方式）；句意是传教士试图使那些偏远岛屿文明起来。

senses.title: To develop a society
senses.definition: to bring a society to a more advanced stage with cities, writing and law
senses.definitionCN: 把一个社会带向有城市、文字与法律的更发达阶段
senses.example: Trade routes helped civilize the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 商路帮助沿海地区走向文明。
senses.why: The verb names the act of pushing a group towards the civilized state.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指推动一个群体走向文明状态的行为。

senses.title: To teach good manners
senses.definition: to make a person or group behave with polite and educated habits
senses.definitionCN: 使人或群体养成礼貌而有教养的习惯
senses.example: Years abroad had civilized his table manners.
senses.exampleCN: 多年在外的经历让他的餐桌礼仪变得文雅。
senses.why: Good manners were treated as a small private version of the same process.
senses.whyCN: 良好举止被视为同一过程在私人层面的小版本。

intro.en: The verb is the action behind civilization, built on the Latin word for a citizen.
intro.cn: 这个动词是文明背后的动作，建立在拉丁语表示公民的词上。

items.en: Civilis meant of a citizen.
items.cn: civilis 意为公民的。

items.en: Civiliser meant to make civil or fit for society.
items.cn: civiliser 意为使变得文明或适合社会。

items.en: English took the verb as civilize and kept the French sense.
items.cn: 英语以 civilize 借入这个动词，保留了法语的含义。

items.en: Writers used it for nations as well as for manners.
items.cn: 作家们既用它说民族，也用它说举止。

items.en: The word now often carries a critical tone about outside interference.
items.cn: 这个词如今常带批评外部干预的口气。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the civil family, while the meaning group names acts of improving people.
note.cn: 形近组列出 civil 家族，近义组列出使人变好的各种动作。

entries.definition: polite, or relating to citizens
entries.definitionCN: 有礼的，或与公民有关的

entries.definition: a person who is not in the armed forces
polite behaviour or a polite remark
to teach someone over a long period
to improve something by small changes
entries.definitionCN: 通过细微改变来改善某物

entries.definition: to give someone knowledge and understanding

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the citizen root, the -ize ending and the contrast between nations and manners.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用公民词根、-ize 后缀以及民族与举止的对比。

normal.en: Civilize is civil plus -ize, so it means to make something civil.
normal.cn: civilize 是 civil 加 -ize，所以意思是使某物变得文明。

normal.en: The verb is transitive: someone always civilizes someone else.
normal.cn: 这个动词是及物的：总是一方教化另一方。

normal.en: Nations can be civilized, and so can table manners.
normal.cn: 民族可以被开化，餐桌礼仪也可以变得文雅。

normal.en: The -ize ending marks an action, while -ization marks the resulting process or state.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ize 表示动作，-ization 表示由此形成的过程或状态。

normal.en: Modern writers often avoid the verb because it sounds one-sided.
normal.cn: 现代作家常避开这个动词，因为它听起来居高临下。

abstract.en: Picture a road and a school appearing together on an empty plain.
abstract.cn: 想象空旷平原上同时出现一条路和一所学校。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor correcting a child's grip on a fork.
abstract.cn: 想象一位客人纠正孩子拿叉子的手势。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the shaded area slowly spreads inland.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上着色区域慢慢向内陆扩展。

examples.en: The school tried to civilize the children of the frontier.
examples.cn: 这所学校试图教化边疆地区的孩子。

examples.en: He was civilized by years of travel and good company.
examples.cn: 多年的旅行与良好的交往让他变得文雅。

examples.en: Missionaries came to civilize the islanders and stayed to learn from them.
examples.cn: 传教士来教化岛民，后来却留下来向他们学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 civil 想成「市民的」，ize 想成「使」：使人都像市民那样守规矩，就是教化。

root: 源自拉丁语 civilis（公民的），经法语 civiliser 进入英语，字面意思是使某人变得像公民一样守秩序。

sensesIntro.en: The verb first improves a whole society, then a single person's manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词先指改善整个社会，再指改善个人的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road, a school and a court rising on open land.
core.cn: 核心意象：开阔土地上同时立起道路、学校与法庭。

branches.en: The verb pushes a whole society towards cities and law.
branches.cn: 这个动词把整个社会推向城市与法律。

branches.en: The same verb polishes the manners of one person.
branches.cn: 同一个动词也打磨个人的举止。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of making someone fit for society.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享让某人适合社会的意思。

branches.en: Trade and schools do the work that the verb describes.
branches.cn: 贸易与学校承担了这个动词所描述的工作。

branches.en: Manners are the small private form of the public process.
branches.cn: 举止是这一公共过程在私人层面的小形态。

intro.en: The verb base takes the -ize ending and grows a noun and two adjectives.
intro.cn: 这个动词词基接 -ize 后缀，并长出名词与两个形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin civilis, so the verb belongs to the same citizen family as civil and civilian.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 civilis，因此这个动词与 civil、civilian 同属公民家族。

items.meaning: to bring a society to a developed stage
items.example: Steam ships helped civilize the coast.
items.exampleCN: 汽船帮助沿海走向文明。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.exampleCN: 贸易很快使港口文明起来。

items.example: The railway civilized the valley in ten years.
items.exampleCN: 铁路在十年间使山谷文明起来。

items.meaning: used for perfect tenses and the passive
items.meaningCN: 用于完成时与被动语态
items.example: The region was civilized by settlers.
items.exampleCN: 这一地区被移民开化了。

items.example: They were civilizing the frontier slowly.
The verb gave birth to civilization.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词孕育出文明一词。
礼貌的回答不花什么成本。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示使之怎样的动词

latinEntries.example: Civilis is the base of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: civilis 是整个家族的词基。

definition_zh: 声称；断言；索取；认领；主张；权利要求
definition_en: to say that something is true when others may doubt it, to ask for something as your right, or a right that you say you have
core_image: 一只手举着一张写有自己名字的单据
scene: 保险员把表格推过来，笔尖停在签名处。Two men claim the same wallet at the front desk.
sceneCN: 这里 claim 指「认领」（第 2 个义项：主张某物归自己所有）；句意是两个男人在前台都声称那个钱包是自己的。

senses.title: To state as true
senses.definition: to say that something is true when other people may not believe it
senses.definitionCN: 在别人可能不相信时仍说某事为真
senses.example: She claims the keys were left on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她声称钥匙是落在桌子上的。
senses.why: The old verb meant to cry out, so a claim is something said loudly and publicly.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老动词本指大声喊出，因此 claim 是被大声公开说出来的话。

senses.title: To demand as your own
senses.definition: to ask for something that you believe belongs to you by right
senses.definitionCN: 要求得到你认为按权利属于自己的东西
senses.example: He claimed his luggage at the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 他在柜台认领了自己的行李。
senses.why: A public cry for something became a formal demand for property or payment.
senses.whyCN: 公开喊出某物，演变成对财产或款项的正式要求。

senses.title: A right or a demand
senses.definition: a statement that you have a right to something, or that right itself
senses.definitionCN: 关于你有权得到某物的声明，或该项权利本身
senses.example: Her claim to the land was never proved.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这块土地的所有权主张从未得到证实。
senses.why: The noun took the same shape as the verb and named the demand rather than the act of demanding.
senses.whyCN: 名词与动词同形，但它指所提的要求，而不是提出要求的动作。

intro.en: Claim comes from a Latin verb meaning to cry out, which also gave English exclaim and proclaim.
intro.cn: claim 出自拉丁语中表示大声喊出的动词，exclaim 与 proclaim 也来自它。

items.en: Clamare meant to cry out or call loudly.
items.cn: clamare 意为大声喊叫或呼喊。

items.en: Clamer carried the sense of calling out a demand.
items.cn: clamer 带有喊出一项要求的含义。

items.en: English took the word as claimen in law and argument.
items.cn: 英语以 claimen 的形式把它用于法律与辩论。

items.en: A claim became a formal demand for land or money.
items.cn: claim 成为对土地或金钱的正式要求。

items.en: The verb widened to plain statements of fact.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到对事实的普通陈述。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words with a similar shape, while the meaning group holds verbs of saying and demanding.
note.cn: 形近组列出外形相近的短词，近义组列出言说与要求类动词。

entries.definition: a tool that holds things tightly together
entries.definitionCN: 把东西紧紧夹住的工具

entries.definition: to hold something firmly with your hand
to praise someone loudly and publicly
to state something firmly as a fact
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地把某事说成事实

entries.definition: to announce something officially or clearly
entries.definitionCN: 正式或清楚地宣布某事

entries.definition: to ask for something very firmly

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cry-out root, the legal demand and the noun-verb pair.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用呼喊词根、法律要求以及名动同形这三条线。

normal.en: Claim belongs with exclaim and proclaim; all three contain the Latin cry for a call.
normal.cn: claim 与 exclaim、proclaim 同族，三者都含拉丁语表示喊叫的部分。

normal.en: To claim is to put your hand up in public, either to speak or to take.
normal.cn: claim 就是在公开场合举手，要么发言，要么拿东西。

normal.en: The noun and the verb look the same, so a claim is both the act and the thing demanded.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 claim 既是动作，也是所要求的对象。

normal.en: Insurance papers are full of claims, because a claim asks for money.
normal.cn: 保险文件里满是 claim，因为这个词可以指索赔。

normal.en: Lay claim to is the fixed phrase for ownership, not for an opinion.
normal.cn: lay claim to 是表示所有权的固定说法，不用来说看法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised at an auction with a numbered card.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖会上举起一只拿着号牌的手。

abstract.en: Picture a luggage tag matching the name on a passport.
abstract.cn: 想象一张行李牌与护照上的名字对得上。

abstract.en: Picture a boundary line drawn on a map and then disputed.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画出一条边界线，随后被人争执。

examples.en: She claims the keys were left on the desk.
examples.cn: 她声称钥匙是落在桌子上的。

examples.en: He claimed his luggage at the counter before the taxi came.
examples.cn: 出租车来之前，他在柜台认领了行李。

examples.en: The company made a claim for the damaged goods.
examples.cn: 公司就受损货物提出了索赔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「喊」，aim 想成「目标」：朝着目标喊一声，就是声明这东西归我。

root: 源自拉丁语 clamare（大声喊叫），经古法语 clamer 进入英语，本义是喊出自己的权利。

sensesIntro.en: A loud cry turns into an assertion, then into a demand, and finally into the right behind the demand.
sensesIntro.cn: 一声大喊先变成断言，再变成索求，最后变成索求背后的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand holding a paper with a name on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手拿着写有名字的纸。

branches.en: The old cry becomes a public statement of fact.
branches.cn: 古老的呼喊变成公开的事实陈述。

branches.en: The same cry becomes a request for what is yours.
branches.cn: 同样的呼喊变成对属于自己之物的索求。

branches.en: The noun names the demand and the right behind it.
branches.cn: 名词指所提的要求以及其背后的权利。

branches.en: Saying and taking share one verb because both are public acts.
branches.cn: 言说与索取共用一个动词，因为两者都是公开行为。

branches.en: A claim needs a right, and a right survives only if claimed.
branches.cn: 索求需要权利，而权利只有被主张才存在。

intro.en: One short verb grows a plural, two participles, an agent noun and two prefixed forms.
intro.cn: 一个短动词长出复数、两个分词、一个施动名词和两个前缀形式。

latinIntro.en: The base clamare also underlies exclaim, proclaim and acclaim, all built with Latin prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 clamare 也是 exclaim、proclaim、acclaim 的来源，这些词都加了拉丁语前缀。

items.meaning: to state true or demand as a right

definition_zh: 拍手；鼓掌；轻拍；拍击声
definition_en: to hit your hands together to show praise, to touch someone lightly with a flat hand, or a sharp sound of this kind
core_image: 两掌相击，声音在剧场里炸开
scene: 演出结束，孩子们从座位上站起来。The audience began to clap as the curtain fell.
sceneCN: 这里 clap 指「拍手；鼓掌」（第 1 个义项：两手相击以表示赞赏）；句意是幕布落下时观众开始鼓掌。

senses.title: To strike hands together
senses.definition: to hit your open hands together again and again to show praise
senses.definitionCN: 反复把张开的两手相击以表示赞赏
senses.example: The whole hall clapped when she finished.
senses.exampleCN: 她讲完时整个大厅都在鼓掌。
senses.why: A flat hand hitting a flat hand makes a sharp sound that carries, so it became the cheapest way to applaud.
senses.whyCN: 平掌击平掌会发出传得远的脆响，因此成了最省事的喝彩方式。

senses.title: To pat lightly
senses.definition: to touch a person or thing quickly with a flat hand
senses.definitionCN: 用平手快速碰一下人或物
senses.example: She clapped him on the shoulder and laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 她拍拍他的肩膀笑了起来。
senses.why: The same flat-hand movement used for applause also serves for a friendly pat.
senses.whyCN: 鼓掌用的那个平掌动作，也用来表示友好的轻拍。

senses.title: A sharp sound
senses.definition: a sudden loud noise, especially one made by hands or by thunder
senses.definitionCN: 突然的巨响，尤指手拍击或雷声
senses.example: A clap of thunder shook the windows.
senses.exampleCN: 一声雷响震得窗户直晃。
senses.why: The noun simply names the sound that the verb produces.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接指这个动词所发出的声音。

intro.en: Clap is an old English sound word, imitating the noise of a flat impact.
intro.cn: clap 是古英语里的拟声词，模仿平拍一下的响声。

items.en: Clappian meant to beat or strike with a flat hand.
items.cn: clappian 意为用平手拍打或击打。

items.en: The word kept the hand sense and added the sound sense.
items.cn: 这个词保留了手部动作义，又加上了声音义。

items.en: Clapping became the usual word for applause in theatres.
items.cn: clapping 成为剧场里表示喝彩的常用词。

items.en: The thunder sense grew from the same sharp noise.
items.cn: 雷声义从同一种脆响引申而来。

items.en: The verb still covers both applause and a friendly pat.
items.cn: 这个动词至今兼指鼓掌与友好轻拍。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words beginning with cl, while the meaning group names ways of striking or praising.
note.cn: 形近组列出以 cl 开头的短词，近义组列出击打与赞扬的方式。

to hold something firmly in your hand

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the onomatopoeic sound, the applause sense and the thunder sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拟声、鼓掌义与雷声义。

normal.en: Clap sounds like what it means: one flat crack, then another.
normal.cn: clap 的读音就像它的意思：啪的一下，又一下。

normal.en: The double p keeps the vowel short, so clap rhymes with map.
normal.cn: 双写 p 让元音保持短音，所以 clap 与 map 押韵。

normal.en: Applause, a friendly pat and a thunder crack all share the same flat impact.
normal.cn: 掌声、友好的轻拍和雷响都共享同一种平拍冲击。

normal.en: Clap your hands is the base phrase; clap him on the back adds the place.
normal.cn: clap your hands 是基本说法，clap him on the back 则补出部位。

normal.en: Clapping is the activity, a clap is one single strike.
normal.cn: clapping 是持续的动作，a clap 是单独的一下。

abstract.en: Picture a dark theatre where a thousand palms meet at once.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗的剧场里一千只手掌同时相击。

abstract.en: Picture a coach's hand landing twice on a player's shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象教练的手在球员肩上落下两下。

abstract.en: Picture a summer sky splitting open above a cornfield.
abstract.cn: 想象夏日天空在玉米地上空裂开一声响。

examples.en: The whole hall clapped when she finished.
examples.cn: 她讲完时整个大厅都在鼓掌。

examples.en: He clapped me on the back and told me to relax.
examples.cn: 他拍拍我的背，让我放松点。

examples.en: A single clap of thunder sent the children indoors.
examples.cn: 一声雷响把孩子们赶进了屋里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「脆」，ap 想成「啊啪」：脆脆的一啊啪，就是拍手声。

root: 源自古英语 clappian（用平手拍打），属于拟声来源的动词，后引申出掌声与雷声等名词义。

sensesIntro.en: One flat impact gives applause, then a friendly pat, and finally the sound itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次平拍先带来鼓掌，再变成友好轻拍，最后成为声音本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two open palms meeting in a sharp crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只张开的手掌相击，发出一声脆响。

branches.en: Repeated strikes of the palms become applause.
branches.cn: 手掌反复相击就成了鼓掌。

branches.en: One soft strike becomes a friendly pat.
branches.cn: 一次轻击就成了友好的拍抚。

branches.en: The noise itself is named by the same word.
branches.cn: 声音本身也用同一个词表示。

branches.en: Applause and thunder share the sharpness of the sound.
branches.cn: 掌声与雷声共享这种声音的脆利感。

branches.en: Both hand senses depend on a flat palm.
branches.cn: 两个与手有关的义项都依赖平掌动作。

intro.en: The short verb doubles its final consonant and grows an agent noun and a noun of action.
intro.cn: 这个短动词双写末尾辅音，并长出施动名词与动作名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here: clap is a native imitative word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语词基：clap 是英语本族的拟声词。

A burst of clapping filled the room.

definition_zh: 澄清；阐明；使（液体）变清
definition_en: to make something easier to understand, or to make a liquid clear by removing the solids in it
core_image: 浑水静置后慢慢变透明
scene: 会议开到一半，投影上的数字互相矛盾。She asked him to clarify the second point before the vote.
sceneCN: 这里 clarify 指「澄清；阐明」（第 1 个义项：把不清楚的事说明白）；句意是她让他在表决前把第二点讲清楚。

senses.title: To make something understandable
senses.definition: to explain something so that it becomes clear and easy to understand
senses.definitionCN: 加以解释，使某事变得清楚易懂
senses.example: The teacher clarified the rule with one example.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用一个例子把这个规则讲清楚了。
senses.why: The Latin base means bright, so to clarify is literally to make a matter bright.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基本义是明亮的，所以 clarify 字面上就是让事情变亮。

senses.title: To clear a liquid
senses.definition: to make a liquid clear by heating it or removing the solid bits
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热或去除固体微粒使液体变清
senses.example: Melt the butter and clarify it slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 把黄油化开，慢慢澄清。
senses.why: The same brightness image applies to a cloudy liquid that turns transparent.
senses.whyCN: 同样的明亮意象也用于由浑浊变透明的液体。

intro.en: Clarify is built on the Latin adjective for bright, the same root as clarity and clear.
intro.cn: clarify 建立在拉丁语表示明亮的形容词上，与 clarity、clear 同根。

items.en: Clarus meant bright, clear or famous.
items.cn: clarus 意为明亮的、清澈的或闻名的。

items.en: Clarificare meant to make bright or to make plain.
items.cn: clarificare 意为使明亮或使明白。

items.en: Clarifier carried the sense of explaining and of clearing liquid.
items.cn: clarifier 兼有解释与澄清液体的含义。

items.en: English took the verb as clarify in learned and kitchen use.
items.cn: 英语以 clarify 借入，用于学术与厨房两种场合。

items.en: The explaining sense now dominates in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 在日常语言中，解释义如今占主导。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the clarity family, while the meaning group names ways of making things plain.
note.cn: 形近组列出 clarity 家族，近义组列出使事情明白的各种说法。

entries.definition: the quality of being clear and easy to follow
easy to see through or to understand
entries.definitionCN: 容易看透或容易理解的

entries.definition: an explanation that removes doubt
to tell someone how something works
entries.definitionCN: 告诉某人某事如何运作

entries.definition: to make something less complicated
to light something up or make it clear

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the bright root, the cloudy-liquid image and the -ify ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用明亮词根、浑浊液体的意象以及 -ify 后缀。

normal.en: Clarify shares its root with clear and clarity: all three carry brightness.
normal.cn: clarify 与 clear、clarity 同根，三者都带明亮的含义。

normal.en: To clarify is to switch on a lamp in a room where people are guessing.
normal.cn: clarify 就是在大家靠猜的房间里打开一盏灯。

normal.en: The -ify ending means to make, so clarify means to make clear.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ify 表示使成为，所以 clarify 就是使清楚。

normal.en: Butter can be clarified, and so can an argument.
normal.cn: 黄油可以澄清，争论也可以澄清。

normal.en: In meetings, clarify a point is more polite than you are wrong.
normal.cn: 在会上说 clarify a point 比说你错了要客气。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of muddy water settling until the light passes through.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯浑水静置到光线能透过去。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing one line on a crowded whiteboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在写满字的黑板上划出其中一行。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp switched on above a table of confused faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一张困惑面孔围坐的桌子上方亮起一盏灯。

examples.en: The teacher clarified the rule with one example.
examples.cn: 老师用一个例子把这个规则讲清楚了。

examples.en: Could you clarify what the second figure means?
examples.cn: 你能说明第二个数字是什么意思吗？

examples.en: Melt the butter and clarify it slowly.
examples.cn: 把黄油化开，慢慢澄清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 clar 想成「clear 的兄弟」，ify 想成「使」：使事情清楚，就是澄清。

root: 源自拉丁语 clarus（明亮的、清楚的）与 clarificare（使明亮），经法语 clarifier 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One brightness image serves both a puzzling sentence and a cloudy liquid.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个明亮意象既用于难懂的句子，也用于浑浊的液体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: muddy water settling until it turns transparent.
core.cn: 核心意象：浑水静置，慢慢变得透明。

branches.en: Brightness becomes ease of understanding.
branches.cn: 明亮变成易于理解。

branches.en: The same brightness clears a cloudy liquid.
branches.cn: 同一种明亮感也让浑浊液体变清。

branches.en: Both senses remove whatever blocks the view.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在去除挡住视线的东西。

branches.en: An example works like light on a confusing rule.
branches.cn: 例子就像照在难懂规则上的光。

branches.en: Heat separates the solids and leaves the clear part.
branches.cn: 加热分离出固体，留下清澈的部分。

intro.en: The verb base takes -ify and grows a noun of quality, a noun of action and an instrument noun.
intro.cn: 这个动词词基接 -ify，并长出性质名词、动作名词与工具名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin clarus, bright, which also underlies clear, clarity and declare.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 clarus（明亮的），clear、clarity、declare 也源于它。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.exampleCN: 她的便条把这个规则讲清楚了。

items.example: He clarified the figures at once.

items.exampleCN: 她正在说明自己的立场。

items.example: The report is praised for its clarity.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告因清晰而受称赞。

items.example: We asked for a short clarification.

items.meaningCN: 使液体变清的设备或药剂
items.example: The tank has a clarifier at the bottom.

items.meaning: forming verbs that mean to make
items.meaningCN: 构成表示使之怎样的动词

latinEntries.example: Clarus is the root of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clarus 是整个家族的词根。

definition_zh: 冲突；抵触；（颜色、日程）不协调；撞击声
definition_en: to fight or disagree strongly, to look wrong together or happen at the same time, or a loud noise of metal hitting metal
core_image: 两面金属盾牌在半空相撞，火星四溅
scene: 两个人站在走廊两头，谁也不肯让路。Their views clash whenever the budget comes up.
sceneCN: 这里 clash 指「冲突；抵触」（第 1 个义项：意见或利益尖锐对立）；句意是每次谈到预算，他们的看法就冲突。

senses.title: A fight or strong disagreement
senses.definition: a short fight or a sharp disagreement between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体之间的短暂打斗或尖锐分歧
senses.example: A clash broke out between the two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 两个群体之间爆发了冲突。
senses.why: The sound of weapons meeting became the name of the meeting itself.
senses.whyCN: 兵器相击的声音，变成了这场相遇本身的名称。

senses.title: A bad match in time or colour
senses.definition: to look wrong together, or to be fixed for the same time as something else
senses.definitionCN: 放在一起显得不协调，或与另一事排在同一时间
senses.example: My lecture clashes with the football final.
senses.exampleCN: 我的讲座和足球决赛撞时间了。
senses.why: Two things that cannot sit together are said to strike each other, like metal on metal.
senses.whyCN: 无法并存的两件事被说成互相撞击，就像金属碰金属。

senses.title: A loud metallic noise
senses.definition: a hard, ringing sound made when metal objects hit each other
senses.definitionCN: 金属物件相撞时发出的刺耳响声
senses.example: The clash of the gates echoed down the street.
senses.exampleCN: 铁门的撞击声在街上传开。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the word began as an imitation of that noise.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：这个词最初就是模仿那种响声。

intro.en: Clash began as an imitative word for the noise of metal or weapons meeting.
intro.cn: clash 最初是模仿金属或兵器相撞之声的拟声词。

items.en: The word imitated a hard ringing impact.
items.cn: 这个词模仿坚硬物体相击的响声。

items.en: Clash named the noise of swords and armour.
items.cn: clash 指刀剑与甲片相击的声音。

items.en: The noun widened to any short fight.
items.cn: 名词扩展到任何短促的打斗。

items.en: Writers used it for disagreements of opinion.
items.cn: 作家们用它表示意见分歧。

items.en: The word now also covers colours and timetables.
items.cn: 这个词如今也用于颜色与日程。

note.en: The look-alike group holds noisy words with a similar ending, while the meaning group names open disagreements.
note.cn: 形近组列出结尾相近的声响词，近义组列出公开的分歧。

entries.definition: a violent collision or a loud breaking noise
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈的碰撞或破碎巨响

entries.definition: to hold something firmly
the sound of liquid hitting a surface
a serious disagreement that lasts some time
entries.definitionCN: 持续一段时间的严重分歧

entries.definition: an accident in which two moving things hit
entries.definitionCN: 两个运动物体相撞的事故

entries.definition: an angry argument between people who know each other

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the metallic sound, the timetable sense and the colour sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用金属声响、日程义与颜色义。

normal.en: Clash sounds like two cymbals: one hard hit, then ringing.
normal.cn: clash 听起来像两面钹：硬碰一下，然后余响。

normal.en: The word began with weapons, so every clash keeps a little violence.
normal.cn: 这个词起于兵器，所以每个 clash 都带一点火药味。

normal.en: Two meetings can clash, and so can a green shirt and red trousers.
normal.cn: 两场会可以撞时间，绿衬衫和红裤子也可以不搭。

normal.en: Clash with is the usual pattern: clash with a plan, clash with a colour.
normal.cn: clash with 是常用搭配：与计划冲突、与颜色不搭。

normal.en: A clash is shorter than a conflict and louder than a quarrel.
normal.cn: clash 比 conflict 短促，比 quarrel 更响亮。

abstract.en: Picture two shields meeting in mid-air with a spray of sparks.
abstract.cn: 想象两面盾牌在半空相撞，火星四溅。

abstract.en: Picture two calendars with the same evening blocked out twice.
abstract.cn: 想象两本日历上同一个晚上被圈了两次。

abstract.en: Picture a green scarf laid on a red coat and quickly taken away.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿围巾放在红大衣上，又赶紧被拿走。

examples.en: A clash broke out between the two groups at the gate.
examples.cn: 两个群体在大门口爆发了冲突。

examples.en: My lecture clashes with the football final.
examples.cn: 我的讲座和足球决赛撞时间了。

examples.en: The clash of the gates echoed down the empty street.
examples.cn: 铁门的撞击声在空街上回荡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「磕」，ash 想成「灰」：磕出灰来，就是撞得很响的冲突。

root: 源自英语本族的拟声词，模仿金属相击的脆响，后由声音义引申为打斗、意见冲突与不协调。

sensesIntro.en: A metallic noise becomes a fight, then a disagreement, then any two things that cannot fit together.
sensesIntro.cn: 金属响声先变成打斗，再变成意见冲突，最后变成任何无法并存的两件事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two metal shields striking with a spray of sparks.
core.cn: 核心意象：两面金属盾牌相撞，火星四溅。

branches.en: The noise of weapons becomes the fight itself.
branches.cn: 兵器之声变成了打斗本身。

branches.en: Things that cannot share a space seem to strike each other.
branches.cn: 无法共存的事物仿佛在互相撞击。

branches.en: The original sound sense stays in the noun.
branches.cn: 最初的声音义仍保留在名词里。

branches.en: Both senses keep the hardness of metal.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了金属的硬度感。

branches.en: A fight and a bad match share the idea of collision.
branches.cn: 打斗与不搭共享碰撞这一概念。

intro.en: The verb base adds -es, -ed and -ing, and forms one compound noun.
intro.cn: 这个动词词基接 -es、-ed、-ing，并构成一个复合名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base: clash is a native imitative word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语词基：clash 是英语本族的拟声词。

definition_zh: 班级；课；阶级；类别；等级
definition_en: a group of students taught together, a lesson, a social rank, or a group of things of the same type
core_image: 一间教室里按排坐好的学生，黑板写着课表
scene: 铃声响过，走廊一下空了，只有一间教室还亮着灯。She stayed behind after class to ask a question.
sceneCN: 这里 class 指「课」（第 1 个义项：按班级进行的一节课）；句意是下课后她留下来问了一个问题。

senses.title: A group of students or a lesson
senses.definition: a group of students taught together, or a period of teaching

items.en: English used class for school groups and for ranks of society.

senses.example: The classification of the finds took a whole winter.
senses.exampleCN: 给这些出土物分类花了整整一个冬天。
senses.why: The noun of action simply names what the verb classify does.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作名词直接指 classify 这个动词所做的事。

senses.title: A group produced by sorting
senses.definition: one of the groups that result from sorting things
senses.definitionCN: 分类之后形成的其中一组
senses.example: These tools fall into a separate classification.
senses.exampleCN: 这些工具属于另一个类别。
senses.why: Once the sorting is finished, each box in the result takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 分类完成后，结果中的每一个格子也叫同一个名字。

senses.title: A system of groups
senses.definition: the whole scheme by which a subject is divided into ordered groups
senses.definitionCN: 把某学科划分成有序各组的整套方案
senses.example: The library uses a simple classification.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆采用一套简单的分类法。
senses.why: A set of related groups becomes a system, and the system keeps the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 相关的各组构成体系，而这个体系仍沿用那个动作的名称。

intro.en: Classification joins the class root to the Latin suffix for making a noun of action.
intro.cn: classification 把 class 词根与拉丁语构成动作名词的后缀结合起来。

items.en: Classis meant a division or a class.
items.cn: classis 意为划分或等级。

items.en: Facere meant to make, so the pair meant to make groups.
items.cn: facere 意为做，两者合起来意为做出分组。

items.en: Classification named the new science of sorting plants.
items.cn: classification 指新兴的植物分类之学。

items.en: English borrowed the word for any ordered grouping.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，指任何有序分组。

items.en: It now covers library systems, jobs and secret files.
items.cn: 它如今涵盖图书系统、职位与机密文件。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the classify family, while the meaning group names the results of sorting.
note.cn: 形近组列出 classify 家族，近义组列出分类的结果。

entries.definition: to arrange things into groups
a person or tool that sorts things
entries.definitionCN: 给事物分类的人或工具

entries.definition: arranged in groups, or officially secret
entries.definitionCN: 已分组的，或官方保密的

entries.definition: a group of things of one kind
a set of things placed together
the act of arranging things by kind
entries.definitionCN: 按种类整理事物的动作

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the class root, the -ification ending and the library image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 class 词根、-ification 后缀与图书馆意象。

normal.en: Classification is class plus -ification, so it is literally the making of classes.
normal.cn: classification 是 class 加 -ification，字面上就是造出类别。

normal.en: The word names three things in turn: the act, one resulting group and the whole system.
normal.cn: 这个词依次指三样东西：动作、一个结果组以及整套体系。

normal.en: Biology lives on classification, from kingdom down to species.
normal.cn: 生物学离不开分类，从界一直到种。

normal.en: A classified document is not sorted; it is marked secret.
normal.cn: a classified document 不是分好类的文件，而是标为机密的文件。

normal.en: The verb is classify, the doer is classifier, the result is classification.
normal.cn: 动词是 classify，执行者是 classifier，结果是 classification。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet of drawers, each with a printed label and a number.
abstract.cn: 想象一个抽屉柜，每个抽屉都贴着打印标签和编号。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of leaves sorted into two trays by shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆叶子按形状分进两个托盘。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf where every spine carries the same small code.
abstract.cn: 想象图书馆书架，每本书脊上都有同样的小编码。

examples.en: The classification of the finds took a whole winter.
examples.cn: 给这些出土物分类花了整整一个冬天。

examples.en: These tools fall into a separate classification.
examples.cn: 这些工具属于另一个类别。

examples.en: The library uses a simple classification for all its maps.
examples.cn: 这家图书馆对所有地图采用一套简单的分类法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 class 想成「类」，ification 想成「化过程」：把东西归成类的过程，就是分类。

root: 由拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）组合而成，经法语进入英语，本义是做出分组。

sensesIntro.en: First the act, then a single group, and finally the whole ordered system.
sensesIntro.cn: 先指动作，再指单个组，最后指整套有序体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: labelled drawers holding sorted specimens.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着标签、装好分类标本的抽屉。

branches.en: The act of sorting is the first meaning.
branches.cn: 分类这个动作是第一层含义。

branches.en: Each finished group takes the same name.
branches.cn: 每个分好的组也叫同一个名字。

branches.en: The set of groups becomes a system.
branches.cn: 各组汇合起来成为体系。

branches.en: The act and its result differ only by a finished edge.
branches.cn: 动作与结果只差一个完成的边界。

branches.en: Groups become a system once their order is fixed.
branches.cn: 各组一旦固定次序就成了体系。

intro.en: The noun base grows a verb, two adjectives and an agent noun.
intro.cn: 这个名词词基长出动词、两个形容词与一个施动名词。

latinIntro.en: The base joins Latin classis, a division, with facere, to make.
latinIntro.cn: 词基把拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）结合起来。

items.meaning: the act or result of sorting
more than one category or system

items.example: We classify the rocks by origin.
items.exampleCN: 我们按成因给岩石分类。

items.meaningCN: 已分类的，或标为机密的

items.meaning: a person or device that sorts

items.example: Each class has its own label.

latinEntries.exampleCN: classis 是 classification 的开头。

definition_zh: 把……分类；把……归入某类；把（文件）列为机密
definition_en: to arrange things into groups by shared features, or to declare official information secret
core_image: 长桌上摊开的标本被一一放进贴标签的盒子
scene: 管理员把新到的化石摊在长桌上。Scientists classify these shells by shape and age.
sceneCN: 这里 classify 指「把……分类」（第 1 个义项：按共同特征把事物归入各组）；句意是科学家按形状与年代给这些贝壳分类。

senses.title: To sort into groups
senses.definition: to put things into groups according to features they share
senses.definitionCN: 按共同特征把事物放进各组
senses.example: The students classified the leaves by shape.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们按形状给叶子分类。
senses.why: The verb joins the Latin word for a division with the verb to make, so it means to make divisions.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把拉丁语表示划分的词与表示做的动词结合，意为造出划分。

senses.title: To mark information secret
senses.definition: to give official papers a security level that limits who may read them
senses.definitionCN: 给官方文件定下保密等级，限制可阅读的人
senses.example: The report was classified for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告被列为机密三十年。
senses.why: A secret file is placed in a restricted class, so the sorting verb took on this official sense.
senses.whyCN: 机密文件被归入受限的等级，于是这个分类动词带上了官方含义。

intro.en: Classify is a learned compound of the Latin words for a division and for making.
intro.cn: classify 是拉丁语表示划分与表示做的两个词构成的学术复合词。

items.en: Classis meant a division or a class.
items.cn: classis 意为划分或等级。

items.en: Facere meant to make or to do.
items.cn: facere 意为制作或做。

items.en: Classifier named the work of sorting plants and minerals.
items.cn: classifier 指给植物与矿物分类的工作。

items.en: English took classify from the French naturalists.
items.cn: 英语从法国博物学家那里借入 classify。

items.en: The verb also came to mean restricting official papers.
items.cn: 这个动词后来又表示限制官方文件的阅读。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that differ by one or two letters, while the meaning group names sorting actions.
note.cn: 形近组列出只差一两个字母的词，近义组列出分类动作。

entries.definition: to make something easier to understand
a group or a lesson
a person or device that sorts things
entries.definitionCN: 给事物分类的人或装置

entries.definition: to put things in order by type
to place something in a named group
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放进有名称的组

entries.definition: to put things in a planned order

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the class root, the -ify ending and the two very different senses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 class 词根、-ify 后缀以及两个差别很大的义项。

normal.en: Classify is class plus -ify, so it means to make classes.
normal.cn: classify 是 class 加 -ify，所以意思是造出类别。

normal.en: Classify by and classify as are the two patterns: by a feature, as a member.
normal.cn: classify by 与 classify as 是两个句型：按某特征分，归为某成员。

normal.en: A classified document has a class of secrecy, not a class of students.
normal.cn: a classified document 有保密等级，不是指学生班级。

normal.en: The noun is classification and the doer is classifier, both from the same verb.
normal.cn: 名词是 classification，执行者是 classifier，都出自这个动词。

normal.en: Scientists classify first and name later.
normal.cn: 科学家先分类，后命名。

abstract.en: Picture a long table of shells with small paper labels beside each pile.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌上摆满贝壳，每堆旁边都有小纸标签。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp folder where every page holds one kind only.
abstract.cn: 想象一本邮票册，每一页只放一个种类。

abstract.en: Picture a folder stamped with a red word and locked in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盖了红字的文件夹被锁进抽屉。

examples.en: The students classified the leaves by shape.
examples.cn: 学生们按形状给叶子分类。

examples.en: These birds are classified as rare in the region.
examples.cn: 这些鸟在该地区被列为稀有。

examples.en: The report was classified for thirty years.
examples.cn: 这份报告被列为机密三十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 class 想成「类」，ify 想成「使」：使东西各归其类，就是分类。

root: 由拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）组合，经法语 classifier 进入英语，本义是做出分组。

sensesIntro.en: One verb sorts objects into groups and also puts secret papers into a restricted class.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动词既把实物分进各组，也把机密文件归入受限等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: specimens laid out and moved into labelled boxes.
core.cn: 核心意象：标本摊开来，被逐一移进贴标签的盒子。

branches.en: The verb makes groups out of mixed things.
branches.cn: 这个动词把混杂之物分成组。

branches.en: Official papers are put into a secrecy class.
branches.cn: 官方文件被放进保密等级。

branches.en: Both senses place something inside a class.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把某物放进某一类。

branches.en: A shared feature is the knife that cuts the groups apart.
branches.cn: 共同特征是切开各组的那把刀。

branches.en: Secrecy is only one class among many.
branches.cn: 保密只是众多类别中的一类。

intro.en: The verb takes -es, -ed and -ing, and feeds the whole classification family.
intro.cn: 这个动词接 -es、-ed、-ing，并衍生出整个 classification 家族。

latinIntro.en: The base pairs Latin classis, a division, with facere, to make.
latinIntro.cn: 词基把拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）配在一起。

items.example: We classify the samples by age.

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.exampleCN: 她给每件新发现物分类。

items.example: They classified the rocks last week.
items.exampleCN: 他们上周把岩石分了类。

items.meaning: a person or device that sorts

items.exampleCN: 这块碎片几乎无法归类。

items.meaning: forming verbs that mean to make
items.meaningCN: 构成表示使之怎样的动词

latinEntries.example: Facere supplies the second half of classify.
latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 提供了 classify 的后半部分。

definition_zh: 教室；课堂（教学环境）
definition_en: a room in a school where a class is taught, or the teaching and learning that happens there
core_image: 黑板、成排课桌和一扇透进光的窗
scene: 下课铃响后，黑板上还留着半道没擦干净的算式。Twenty desks fill the classroom from wall to wall.
sceneCN: 这里 classroom 指「教室」（第 1 个义项：学校里上课的房间）；句意是二十张课桌从墙到墙塞满了这间教室。

senses.title: A room for lessons
senses.definition: a room in a school where a group of pupils is taught
senses.definitionCN: 学校里供一群学生上课的房间
senses.example: The classroom smells of chalk and floor polish.
senses.exampleCN: 这间教室里有粉笔和地板蜡的气味。
senses.why: The compound simply joins the group of pupils to the room that holds them.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词直接把学生群体与容纳他们的房间拼在一起。

senses.title: The setting for teaching
senses.definition: the teaching and learning that takes place in such a room
senses.definitionCN: 在这类房间里开展的教学与学习
senses.example: Technology has changed the classroom as much as the office.
senses.exampleCN: 技术对课堂的改变不亚于对办公室的改变。
senses.why: The room stands for the activity inside it, a common shift from place to practice.
senses.whyCN: 房间被用来代表其中的活动，这是从地点转向实践的常见引申。

intro.en: Classroom is a plain English compound of class and room, coined when schools began to sort pupils by age.
intro.cn: classroom 是 class 与 room 构成的普通英语复合词，在学校开始按年龄分班时出现。

items.en: Classis gave English the word class.
items.cn: classis 给了英语 class 一词。

items.en: Rum meant a space or a room.
items.cn: rum 意为空间或房间。

items.en: Class and room were joined for the schoolroom.
items.cn: class 与 room 组合起来指学校的上课房间。

items.en: The compound spread with public schooling.
items.cn: 随着公共教育普及，这个复合词传播开来。

items.en: It now also names the teaching practice itself.
items.cn: 它如今也指教学实践本身。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other class compounds, while the meaning group names rooms and settings for teaching.
note.cn: 形近组列出其他 class 复合词，近义组列出教学场所与场景。

entries.definition: a pupil in the same class as you
entries.definitionCN: 与你在同一个班的同学

entries.definition: work done by pupils during a lesson
entries.definitionCN: 学生在课上完成的作业

entries.definition: a group of pupils or a lesson
a room used for teaching in a school
entries.definitionCN: 学校里用于教学的房间

entries.definition: a large room for lectures at a college
entries.definitionCN: 大学里讲课用的大房间

entries.definition: a room used for reading and writing

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the compound and use the chalk-and-desks picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子拆开这个复合词，并利用粉笔与课桌的画面。

normal.en: Classroom is class plus room, a room for the class.
normal.cn: classroom 是 class 加 room，即上课用的房间。

normal.en: The stress falls on class, so the two parts stay clearly separate.
normal.cn: 重音落在 class 上，因此两部分听起来界限分明。

normal.en: In the classroom takes the article, unlike in class.
normal.cn: in the classroom 要加冠词，而 in class 不加。

normal.en: The word can stand for the teaching itself, as in technology in the classroom.
normal.cn: 这个词可以代表教学本身，如 technology in the classroom。

normal.en: One stem gives class, classroom, classmate and classwork.
normal.cn: 一个词干长出了 class、classroom、classmate 与 classwork。

abstract.en: Picture a blackboard with a half-erased sum still showing.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上还留着擦了一半的算式。

abstract.en: Picture twenty desks in rows with sunlight on the far wall.
abstract.cn: 想象二十张课桌排成行，阳光落在远墙上。

abstract.en: Picture a teacher's desk with a register and a box of chalk.
abstract.cn: 想象讲台上放着点名册和一盒粉笔。

examples.en: The classroom smells of chalk and floor polish.
examples.cn: 这间教室里有粉笔和地板蜡的气味。

examples.en: Twenty desks fill the classroom from wall to wall.
examples.cn: 二十张课桌从墙到墙塞满了这间教室。

examples.en: Technology has changed the classroom as much as the office.
examples.cn: 技术对课堂的改变不亚于对办公室的改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: class 是「班级」，room 是「房间」：一个班待的房间，就是教室。

root: 由 class（源自拉丁语 classis，划分）与 room（古英语 rum，空间）合成，指按班级上课的房间。

sensesIntro.en: First the room itself, then the teaching that fills it.
sensesIntro.cn: 先指房间本身，再指充满其中的教学活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blackboard, rows of desks and one bright window.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黑板、成排课桌和一扇明亮的窗。

branches.en: The compound names the room that holds a class.
branches.cn: 这个复合词指容纳一个班级的房间。

branches.en: The room stands for the teaching inside it.
branches.cn: 房间被用来代表其中的教学。

branches.en: Place and practice share one word.
branches.cn: 地点与实践共用一个词。

branches.en: Desks and a board are the fixed furniture of the sense.
branches.cn: 课桌与黑板是这个义项的固定配置。

branches.en: Talking about the classroom means talking about how lessons work.
branches.cn: 谈论课堂就是在谈论课怎样进行。

intro.en: Two free words join to make one compound, and the class part feeds further compounds.
intro.cn: 两个自由词合成一个复合词，其中 class 部分又长出更多复合词。

latinIntro.en: Only the first half is Latin, from classis; the second half is native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前半部分来自拉丁语 classis，后半部分是英语本族的古英语词。

items.example: The new wing has eight classrooms.

items.meaning: a group of pupils or a lesson

items.example: A classmate lent me a pen.

items.meaning: a room used for a stated purpose

latinEntries.example: Classis is the first half of classroom.

definition_zh: 从句；分句；（合同、法律的）条款
definition_en: a group of words with its own verb that forms part of a sentence, or a separate condition in a legal document
core_image: 合同上被手指按住的一行小字
scene: 律师把合同推到对面，手指顺着其中一行往下滑。A single clause in the contract decides who pays.
sceneCN: 这里 clause 指「条款」（第 2 个义项：法律文件中的一项独立规定）；句意是合同里的一条条款决定了由谁付款。

senses.title: A part of a sentence
senses.definition: a group of words that contains a verb and forms part of a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 含有动词、构成句子一部分的一组词
senses.example: The sentence has one main clause and two relative clauses.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子有一个主句和两个关系从句。
senses.why: A grammatical clause is a closed unit of meaning, so it took the Latin word for a closing.
senses.whyCN: 语法上的分句是一个闭合的意义单位，因此用了拉丁语表示关闭的词。

senses.title: A condition in a document
senses.definition: a separate item in a contract, treaty or law that states a condition
senses.definitionCN: 合同、条约或法律中规定某项条件的独立条目
senses.example: The contract contains a clause about late payment.
senses.exampleCN: 合同里有一条关于逾期付款的条款。
senses.why: Legal sentences were also divided into closed units, and each item kept the name of a clause.
senses.whyCN: 法律条文同样被分成闭合的单元，每一小条都沿用 clause 之名。

intro.en: Clause comes from a Latin verb meaning to close, and it still means a closed unit of a sentence.
intro.cn: clause 出自拉丁语表示关闭的动词，至今仍指句子中一个闭合的单位。

items.en: Claudere meant to close or shut.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭或合上。

items.en: Clausa meant a closed section of a text.
items.cn: clausa 指文本中闭合的一段。

items.en: Clause carried the legal sense of a proviso.
items.cn: clause 带有条文式的法律含义。

items.en: English used clause in law before it named grammar.
items.cn: 英语先在法律中使用 clause，后用于语法。

items.en: The grammatical sense is now the everyday one.
items.cn: 语法义如今是日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that rhyme or nearly rhyme, while the meaning group names parts of sentences and documents.
note.cn: 形近组列出押韵或近韵的词，近义组列出句子与文件中的成分。

entries.definition: something that makes an event happen
a short stop before continuing
a group of pupils or a lesson
a small group of words without a full verb
entries.definitionCN: 不含完整动词的一小组词

entries.definition: a condition written into a law or contract
entries.definitionCN: 写入法律或合同的某项条件

entries.definition: one of the parts into which a text is divided
entries.definitionCN: 文本被分成的部分之一

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用关闭词根、语法义与合同义。

normal.en: Clause hides the Latin verb to close, so a clause is a closed piece of a sentence.

definition_zh: （鸟兽的）爪；（蟹虾的）钳；用爪抓
definition_en: a sharp curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal, the pincer of a crab, or to scratch with such a nail
core_image: 一只弯钩般的利爪扣住树枝
scene: 猫伏在窗台上，尾巴慢慢摆。The cat dug one claw into the cushion and yawned.
sceneCN: 这里 claw 指「爪」（第 1 个义项：鸟兽脚上弯曲的尖甲）；句意是猫把一只爪子抠进坐垫，打了个哈欠。

senses.title: A sharp curved nail
senses.definition: a hard curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal
senses.definitionCN: 鸟或兽脚上坚硬而弯曲的指甲
senses.example: The owl's claws closed around the branch.
senses.exampleCN: 猫头鹰的爪子扣住了树枝。
senses.why: The old English word named the hooked nail itself, before it named any action.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语词先指弯钩状的甲本身，后来才指动作。

senses.title: A crab's pincer
senses.definition: one of the two pinching limbs of a crab, lobster or scorpion
senses.definitionCN: 蟹、龙虾或蝎子两只可夹合的肢体之一
senses.example: The crab raised one claw above the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 螃蟹在沙上举起一只钳。
senses.why: A pincer is a hooked gripper, so the same word covers the limb of a shellfish.
senses.whyCN: 钳是钩状的抓握器，于是同一个词也覆盖甲壳类的肢体。

senses.title: To scratch with claws
senses.definition: to tear or pull at something with claws or fingers
senses.definitionCN: 用爪或手指撕扯、抓挠某物
senses.example: The dog clawed at the door to get out.
senses.exampleCN: 狗抓着门想出去。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb once people described what the claw does.
senses.whyCN: 当人们开始描述爪子所做的事，名词就转为动词。

intro.en: Claw is an old English word for a hooked nail, unchanged in meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: claw 是古英语里表示钩状甲的词，千年来含义几乎未变。

items.en: Clawu named the nail of a bird or beast.
items.cn: clawu 指鸟兽的指甲。

items.en: The form became claw and also named a pincer.
items.cn: 词形变为 claw，也用来指钳。

items.en: The verb appeared, meaning to tear with claws.
items.cn: 动词形式出现，意为用爪撕抓。

items.en: The word entered figures of speech about struggling upward.
items.cn: 这个词进入表示奋力向上攀爬的比喻。

items.en: Claw covers nails, pincers and the act of scratching.
items.cn: claw 兼指爪、钳与抓挠的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words beginning with cl, while the meaning group names pointed gripping parts.
note.cn: 形近组列出以 cl 开头的短词，近义组列出尖锐的抓握部位。

normal.en: Claw is a hook you can see: curved, hard and pointed.

normal.en: Birds scratch with a claw, crabs pinch with a claw, and both are hooks.

normal.en: Claw your way up keeps the image of pulling yourself with hooked fingers.

normal.en: A claw hammer is named for the split hook that pulls nails.

normal.en: The plural claws serves both the noun and the verb.
normal.cn: 复数 claws 既作名词也作动词形式。

definition_zh: 黏土；陶土；（网球）红土场地
definition_en: heavy sticky earth that can be shaped when wet and baked hard, or a sports surface made of crushed clay
core_image: 转盘上被手指拉高的湿泥坯
scene: 轮盘转起来，手上沾满湿乎乎的土。She pressed a lump of clay into a shallow bowl.
sceneCN: 这里 clay 指「黏土」（第 1 个义项：湿时可塑、烧后变硬的黏性土）；句意是她把一团黏土按成了一个浅碗。

senses.title: Sticky earth for shaping
senses.definition: a heavy sticky earth that becomes soft when wet and hard when baked
senses.definitionCN: 湿时变软、烧后变硬的厚重黏性土
senses.example: The children shaped animals from clay.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用黏土捏动物。
senses.why: The old English word named exactly this sticky earth, and that sense has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语中的这个词正是指这种黏性土，这一含义从未改变。

senses.title: A crushed-clay sports surface
senses.definition: a tennis court surface made of crushed brick or clay
senses.definitionCN: 用碎砖或黏土铺成的网球场地面
senses.example: He plays best on clay.
senses.exampleCN: 他在红土场上打得最好。
senses.why: Players shortened the name of the clay court until the material alone meant the surface.
senses.whyCN: 球员把红土球场的名称缩短，最后材料名本身就指这种场地。

intro.en: Clay is a native English word for sticky earth, with relatives across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: clay 是英语本族词，指黏性土，在日耳曼诸语言中有同源词。

items.en: Clæg meant sticky earth used by potters.
items.cn: clæg 指陶工使用的黏性土。

items.en: The spelling settled as clay.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 clay。

items.en: Writers used clay for the human body in religious prose.
items.cn: 作家在宗教文章中用 clay 指人的身体。

items.en: Brick and tile works made clay a trade word.
items.cn: 砖瓦业使 clay 成为行业词。

items.en: Sports also gave the word a surface sense.
items.cn: 体育又给了这个词场地义。

note.cn: 形近组列出元音或结尾相近的短词，近义组列出各种泥土。

to kill someone or something

normal.en: Clay is what a potter's hands are covered with at the end of the day.
normal.cn: clay 就是陶艺师收工时满手沾着的东西。

normal.en: Wet clay bends, dry clay cracks, fired clay rings.
normal.cn: 湿黏土会弯，干黏土会裂，烧过的陶会响。

normal.en: Clay and clod share a shape and both mean lumpy earth.

normal.en: A clay court is red because crushed brick is mixed in.

normal.en: Clay is uncountable, so one says a lump of clay.
normal.cn: clay 不可数，所以说 a lump of clay。

definition_zh: 干净的；清洁的；彻底的；打扫；清洗
definition_en: free from dirt or marks, complete and thorough, or to remove dirt from something
core_image: 擦过后能照出窗影的桌面
scene: 客人按门铃前，她把最后一本书塞回书架。She wiped the table until it was clean.
sceneCN: 这里 clean 指「干净的」（第 1 个义项：没有污垢或痕迹）；句意是她把桌子擦到干干净净。

senses.title: Free from dirt
senses.definition: not marked or covered with dirt, and safe to use
senses.definitionCN: 没有污迹或污垢、可以放心使用的
senses.example: Wash your hands and keep the kitchen clean.
senses.exampleCN: 洗手，并保持厨房干净。
senses.why: The old English adjective meant free from dirt and also pure, and both senses travelled together.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语形容词既指没有污垢，也指纯净，两个含义一路同行。

senses.title: To remove dirt
senses.definition: to remove dirt from something by washing or wiping
senses.definitionCN: 通过洗或擦去除某物上的污垢
senses.example: He cleaned the windows before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭前他把窗户擦了。
senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb meaning to make something clean.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转为动词，意为使某物变干净。

senses.title: Complete and thorough
senses.definition: done fully, with nothing left out or hidden
senses.definitionCN: 做得彻底，没有遗漏也没有隐瞒
senses.example: The team made a clean break with the old plan.
senses.exampleCN: 团队与旧方案彻底断了关系。
senses.why: Something clean has nothing sticking to it, so a clean break leaves no loose ends.
senses.whyCN: 干净的东西不粘带杂物，因此 clean break 指不留尾巴的切割。

items.cn: clæne 意为干净的、纯净的、清楚的。

definition_zh: 清楚的；明白的；清澈的；晴朗的；清理；清除
definition_en: easy to understand, easy to see through, free of cloud, or to remove things from a place
core_image: 雾散后一条条显出来的山脊
scene: 雾散开，远处的山脊一条条显出来。The sky became clear just before sunset.
sceneCN: 这里 clear 指「晴朗的；清澈的」（第 2 个义项：没有云雾遮挡、透明可见）；句意是日落前天空放晴了。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: expressed in a way that leaves no doubt or confusion
senses.definitionCN: 表达得没有疑问或混乱的
senses.example: Her instructions were short and clear.
senses.exampleCN: 她的指示简短而清楚。
senses.why: The Latin base meant bright, and a bright room lets you see everything without strain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基本义是明亮的，明亮的房间让人不费力就能看清一切。

senses.title: Transparent or cloudless
senses.definition: easy to see through, or free of cloud and mist
senses.definitionCN: 容易看透的，或没有云和雾的
senses.example: The lake was clear down to the stones.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水清得能看见水底的石头。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: nothing stands between the eye and the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义：眼睛与物体之间没有任何遮挡。

senses.title: To remove what blocks
senses.definition: to remove objects or obstacles from a place so that it is free
senses.definitionCN: 把物体或障碍从某处移走使之空出
senses.example: Please clear the boxes from the hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 请把走廊上的箱子清走。
senses.why: To make a place clear is to take away what blocks the view or the way.
senses.whyCN: 使一个地方 clear，就是把挡住视线或通道的东西拿走。

intro.en: Clear comes from the Latin adjective for bright, which also gave clarify and clarity.
intro.cn: clear 出自拉丁语表示明亮的形容词，clarify 与 clarity 也来自它。

items.en: Clarus meant bright, clear or famous.
items.cn: clarus 意为明亮的、清澈的或闻名的。

items.en: Cler meant bright and also free of guilt.
items.cn: cler 意为明亮的，也指无罪的。

items.en: English used clear for light, water and speech.
items.cn: 英语用 clear 形容光、水与言语。

items.en: The verb appeared, meaning to make a place free.
items.cn: 动词形式出现，意为使某处空出来。

items.en: The word now also covers permissions and profits.
items.cn: 这个词如今也用于许可与净利。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the clarity family, while the meaning group names what can be seen or understood easily.
note.cn: 形近组列出 clarity 家族，近义组列出容易看见或理解的状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the bright root, the weather sense and the clearing verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用明亮词根、天气义与清理动词。

normal.en: Clear, clarify and clarity all carry Latin brightness.
normal.cn: clear、clarify、clarity 都带着拉丁语的明亮。

normal.en: A clear sky, clear water and a clear sentence all lack something in the way.
normal.cn: 晴空、清水与清楚的句子，都是路上少了遮挡。

normal.en: To clear a table is to make its surface visible again.
normal.cn: clear a table 就是让桌面重新露出来。

normal.en: Clear up can mean the sky opening or a mess being tidied.
normal.cn: clear up 既可指天放晴，也可指把乱局收拾好。

normal.en: The comparative is clearer, with the r sound doubled in spelling.
normal.cn: 比较级是 clearer，拼写里 r 音连在一起。

abstract.cn: 想象雾气从山脊上一层一层退开。

abstract.en: Picture a lake so transparent that stones look close.
abstract.cn: 想象湖水透明到石头看着很近。

abstract.en: Picture a bare table with only light on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空桌上只剩光。

examples.en: Her instructions were short and clear.
examples.cn: 她的指示简短而清楚。

examples.en: The sky became clear just before sunset.
examples.cn: 日落前天空放晴了。

sensesIntro.en: Brightness first lets you see through, then lets you understand, then lets you remove what blocks.
sensesIntro.cn: 明亮先让你看透，再让你听懂，最后让你把挡路的东西搬走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ridges appearing as mist lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：雾散时山脊一条条显现。

branches.en: Brightness of light becomes brightness of meaning.
branches.cn: 光的明亮变成意义的明白。

branches.en: The physical sense keeps air and water free of cloud.
branches.cn: 具体义指空气与水没有云雾。

branches.en: To clear is to remove what stands in the way.
branches.cn: 清除就是搬走挡路之物。

branches.en: Both let something pass without distortion.
branches.cn: 两者都让某物无失真地通过。

branches.en: A cleared space is as open as a clear sky.
branches.cn: 清空的地方像晴空一样开阔。

intro.en: The short adjective grows a comparative, a verb set and four derived words.
intro.cn: 这个短形容词长出比较级、动词形式以及四个派生词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin clarus, bright, which also underlies clarify and clarity.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 clarus（明亮的），clarify 与 clarity 也源于它。

items.exampleCN: 这是最清楚的一张地图。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject

items.exampleCN: 他每晚都把桌子收拾干净。

definition_zh: 清楚地；明显地；显然
definition_en: in a way that is easy to see, hear or understand, or used to say that something is obviously true
core_image: 一句话穿过整间教室，落到最后一排
scene: 讲解的人放慢速度，每个字都传到最后一排。She spoke clearly enough for everyone at the back.
sceneCN: 这里 clearly 指「清楚地」（第 1 个义项：以容易听清、看懂的方式）；句意是她讲得足够清楚，后排每个人都听得见。

senses.title: In an easy-to-follow way
senses.definition: in a way that is easy to hear, see or understand
senses.definitionCN: 以容易听见、看见或理解的方式
senses.example: Please say your name clearly into the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 请对着电话把名字说清楚。
senses.why: The adverb simply describes how an action is done, and it inherits the brightness of clear.
senses.whyCN: 副词只是描述动作怎样进行，它继承了 clear 的明亮含义。

senses.title: Without any doubt
senses.definition: used to state that something is obviously true
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某事显然为真
senses.example: Clearly, the plan will cost more than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 显然，这个方案的花费会超出预期。
senses.why: What is seen clearly needs no argument, so the adverb came to mark an obvious conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 看得清楚的事无需论证，于是这个副词用来标记显而易见的结论。

intro.en: Clearly is clear plus the old English adverb ending, and it keeps the brightness image.
intro.cn: clearly 是 clear 加古英语副词词尾，保留了明亮的意象。

items.en: Clarus meant bright or clear.
items.cn: clarus 意为明亮的或清楚的。

items.en: The ending -lice turned adjectives into adverbs.
items.cn: 词尾 -lice 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: The ending became -ly and clearly took its place.
items.cn: 词尾变为 -ly，clearly 由此定型。

items.en: Writers used clearly to open an obvious statement.
items.cn: 作家用 clearly 引出一个显而易见的论断。

items.en: The word works both as a manner adverb and a sentence adverb.
items.cn: 这个词既作方式副词，也作句子副词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds forms built on clear, while the meaning group holds adverbs of plainness.
note.cn: 形近组列出由 clear 构成的 forms，近义组列出表示明白的副词。

easier to see or understand

entries.definitionCN: 以任何人都看得出的方式

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ly pattern, the two positions in a sentence and the brightness image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 -ly 构词、句中两个位置以及明亮意象。

normal.en: Clearly is clear plus -ly, so it describes the manner of an action.
normal.cn: clearly 是 clear 加 -ly，描述动作的方式。

normal.en: At the end of a sentence it tells how; at the front it tells you what to conclude.
normal.cn: 放在句末说明怎样做，放在句首告诉你该得出什么结论。

normal.en: Speak clearly is about sound, see clearly is about sight, think clearly is about mind.
normal.cn: speak clearly 关乎声音，see clearly 关乎视觉，think clearly 关乎头脑。

normal.en: Clearly wrong is a polite way to say obviously wrong.
normal.cn: clearly wrong 是 obviously wrong 的客气说法。

normal.en: The word has no comparative form, so one says more clearly.
normal.cn: 这个词没有比较级形式，因此说 more clearly。

abstract.en: Picture a voice crossing a whole classroom and landing at the back row.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音穿过整间教室落到最后一排。

abstract.en: Picture a line of print sharp enough to read from a step away.
abstract.cn: 想象一行字清晰到退开一步仍能读。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifting a curtain so the view is plain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手拉开窗帘，景色一目了然。

examples.en: She spoke clearly enough for everyone at the back.
examples.cn: 她讲得足够清楚，后排每个人都听得见。

examples.en: The sign is clearly visible from the road.
examples.cn: 从路上就能清楚看见这块牌子。

examples.en: Clearly, the plan will cost more than expected.
examples.cn: 显然，这个方案的花费会超出预期。

dict_mnemonic.text: clear 是「清楚」，ly 是「地」：清楚地，就是把话说到人人都懂。

root: 由 clear（源自拉丁语 clarus，明亮的）加古英语副词词尾 -lice（今 -ly）构成。

sensesIntro.en: First the manner of seeing or speaking, then the certainty of a conclusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 先指看或说的方式，再指结论的确定无疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice reaching the last row without effort.
core.cn: 核心意象：声音毫不费力地传到最后一排。

branches.en: The adverb describes a clear manner of acting.
branches.cn: 这个副词描述清楚的行事方式。

branches.en: It also marks a conclusion that needs no proof.
branches.cn: 它也标记无需证明的结论。

branches.en: Both rest on the idea that nothing blocks the view.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在没有遮挡视线这一想法上。

branches.en: Sound, sight and thought can all be done clearly.
branches.cn: 声音、视觉与思考都可以做得清楚。

branches.en: A clearly seen fact ends an argument.
branches.cn: 看清的事实能终止争论。

intro.en: The adverb is built from clear plus -ly and sits in a small family of clear words.
intro.cn: 这个副词由 clear 加 -ly 构成，属于 clear 的小家族。

latinIntro.en: The base goes back through French to Latin clarus, bright.
latinIntro.cn: 词基经法语上溯到拉丁语 clarus（明亮的）。

items.exampleCN: 这篇文章因清晰而受称赞。

items.example: The clearness of the water surprised us.

items.exampleCN: 她把这个规则讲清楚了。

latinEntries.exampleCN: clarus 是 clearly 的远祖。

definition_zh: 职员；办事员；店员；售货员
definition_en: a person who keeps records or does office work, or a person who serves customers in a shop
core_image: 柜台后低头抄写、核对的账本
scene: 柜台前排了几个人，机打的单据一张张吐出来。The bank clerk counted the notes twice.
sceneCN: 这里 clerk 指「职员」（第 1 个义项：在办公室或柜台处理记录与事务的人）；句意是那位银行职员把钞票点了两遍。

senses.title: A person who keeps records
senses.definition: a person employed to keep records, file papers or do other office work
senses.definitionCN: 受雇保管记录、整理文件或做其他办公室事务的人
senses.example: The clerk stamped the form and filed it.
senses.exampleCN: 那位职员在表格上盖了章并归档。
senses.why: The word once meant a clergyman, then any person who could read and write, and later an office worker.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾指教士，后指任何会读写的人，再后来指办公室职员。

senses.title: A shop assistant
senses.definition: a person who serves customers behind a counter, especially in American use
senses.definitionCN: 在柜台后接待顾客的人，尤用于美式英语
senses.example: The clerk wrapped the gift in blue paper.
senses.exampleCN: 店员用蓝纸把礼物包好。
senses.why: Selling behind a counter was also record work, so the same word covered shop staff.
senses.whyCN: 柜台后卖货同样涉及记账，于是同一个词也指店员。

intro.en: Clerk began as the word for a clergyman, since clergy were almost the only people who could read and write.
intro.cn: clerk 起初指教士，因为当时几乎只有教士会读写。

items.en: Kleros meant a lot or a share, including a share of church duty.
items.cn: kleros 意为抽签所得的一份，也包括教会职务的一份。

items.en: Clericus meant a man of the church.
items.cn: clericus 指教会中人。

items.en: Cleric named a priest or a scholar.
items.cn: cleric 指教士或学者。

items.en: Clerk meant a scholar or a secretary, then any office worker.
items.cn: clerk 指学者或书记，后指任何办公人员。

items.en: American use added the shop assistant sense.
items.cn: 美式用法又加上了店员义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds church and writing words, while the meaning group names people who serve at a counter or desk.
note.cn: 形近组列出教会与文书类词，近义组列出在柜台或桌前服务的人。

entries.definition: relating to office work or to clergy
entries.definitionCN: 与办公室工作或教士有关的

entries.definition: the body of people trained for religious work
entries.definitionCN: 受过宗教训练的人员群体

entries.definition: easy to see or understand

entries.definition: a person who greets visitors at a front desk

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the clergy origin, the reading skill and the counter picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用教士来源、读写能力与柜台画面。

normal.en: Clerk and clergy share a root: the clerk was the church's reader and writer.
normal.cn: clerk 与 clergy 同根：当年的 clerk 就是教会里读写的人。

normal.en: Because clerks could read, the word came to mean any keeper of records.

normal.en: Clerical work means paperwork, not church work, in most modern offices.
normal.cn: 在多数现代办公室里，clerical work 指文书工作而非教会工作。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger, an ink pad and a rubber stamp on a high desk.
abstract.cn: 想象高桌上放着账本、印泥和一枚橡皮章。

abstract.en: Picture a queue of people and a printer spitting out receipts.
abstract.cn: 想象排着队的顾客和一台不断吐出单据的打印机。

abstract.en: Picture a man in a black coat copying a letter by hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一位穿黑衣的人手抄一封信。

examples.cn: 店员用蓝纸把礼物包好。

sensesIntro.en: A clergyman becomes a literate secretary, then an office worker, then a shop assistant.

branches.en: The record keeper sits at a desk with paper.
branches.cn: 管记录的人坐在桌前与纸打交道。

branches.en: The counter worker serves customers and keeps accounts.

branches.en: Both senses rest on handling papers and figures.

branches.en: Reading and writing were once the clerk's special skill.

branches.cn: 美式的店员义从柜台记账发展而来。

definition_zh: 聪明的；机灵的；（办法、主意）巧妙的
definition_en: quick at learning and understanding, or skilful and original in the way something is done
core_image: 孩子把厚书垫在椅子上够到高处的柜子
scene: 孩子把椅子拖到柜子前，又垫上一本厚书。It was a clever way to reach the top shelf.

senses.title: Quick at learning
senses.definition: able to learn and understand things quickly and well
senses.definitionCN: 能够又快又好地学会并理解事物的
senses.example: She is clever enough to see the trap.
senses.exampleCN: 她聪明得能看出这个陷阱。
senses.why: The word first described a quick hand or a quick mind, and the mental sense won out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初形容手快或脑子快，后来心智义占了上风。

senses.title: Skilfully thought out
senses.definition: showing skill and imagination in the way a problem is solved
senses.definitionCN: 在解决某个问题的方式上显出技巧与巧思
senses.example: The lock has a clever little catch.
senses.exampleCN: 这把锁有个巧妙的小卡扣。
senses.why: A clever device shows the same quickness as a clever person, but in an object.
senses.whyCN: 巧妙的装置展现了与聪明人同样的机敏，只不过体现在物件上。

intro.en: The origin of clever is uncertain; it appears in Middle English meaning nimble with the hands.
intro.cn: clever 的来源并不确定，中古英语中出现时意为手很灵巧。

items.en: Cliver meant quick and neat with the hands.
items.cn: cliver 意为手上动作快而利落。

items.en: The word spread to the mind as well as the hands.
items.cn: 这个词从手扩展到头脑。

items.en: Clever settled as the everyday word for bright.
items.cn: clever 定型为表示聪明的日常词。

items.en: A critical tone appeared in phrases like too clever.
items.cn: 像 too clever 这样的说法带出了批评口气。

items.en: The word now also praises a neat solution or design.
items.cn: 这个词如今也称赞巧妙的解法或设计。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words with a similar shape but other meanings, while the meaning group names mental sharpness.
note.cn: 形近组列出外形相近但意义不同的词，近义组列出头脑敏锐。

entries.definition: a heavy knife for chopping meat
to split something with a sharp blow
in a smart and skilful way
quick in thinking and learning
intelligent and quick to understand
very clever and original in design
entries.definitionCN: 设计上非常聪明且有创意的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the quick-hands origin, the two senses and the mild warning in too clever.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用手巧来源、两个义项以及 too clever 的轻微警告。

normal.en: Clever began with clever hands and moved to a clever head.
normal.cn: clever 起于手巧，后来转向头脑灵。

normal.en: A clever person and a clever lock show the same neatness.
normal.cn: 聪明的人与巧妙的锁展现同一种利落。

normal.en: Clever is not quite wise: it praises speed, not judgement.
normal.cn: clever 不等于 wise：它称赞的是快，而不是判断力。

normal.en: Too clever by half means someone has outsmarted himself.
normal.cn: too clever by half 指聪明反被聪明误。

normal.en: The comparative doubles nothing: cleverer and cleverest keep one l.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级不加倍写 l：cleverer、cleverest。

abstract.en: Picture a child stacking a thick book on a chair to reach a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子把厚书垫在椅子上够一个罐子。

abstract.en: Picture a lid that opens with one twist and no tools.
abstract.cn: 想象一个一拧就开、不用工具的盖子。

abstract.en: Picture a knot that holds under load and slips free with one pull.
abstract.cn: 想象一个受力不散、一拉就开的绳结。

examples.en: She is clever enough to see the trap.
examples.cn: 她聪明得能看出这个陷阱。

examples.en: It was a clever way to reach the top shelf.
examples.cn: 那是个够到顶层架子的巧妙办法。

examples.en: The lock has a clever little catch.
examples.cn: 这把锁有个巧妙的小卡扣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cle 想成「撬」，ver 想成「弯」：会撬会弯着想法子的人，就是机灵。

root: 中古英语作 cliver，可能源自古英语表示灵巧的词，本义是手快而利落，后转指头脑敏捷。

sensesIntro.en: Quick hands come first, then a quick mind, then a neatly made thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是手快，再是脑快，最后指做得巧妙的物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book stacked on a chair to reach a high shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：把书垫在椅子上够到高架。

branches.en: The old hand sense becomes a quick mind.
branches.cn: 旧日的手巧义变成头脑敏捷。

branches.en: A solution can be clever without being a person.
branches.cn: 解法可以很巧妙，而不必是人。

branches.en: People and devices share the same neat skill.
branches.cn: 人与装置共享同一种利落的技巧。

branches.en: Clever praises speed of learning, not depth of wisdom.
branches.cn: clever 称赞学习快，而不是智慧深。

branches.en: A clever trick may also be slightly dishonest.
branches.cn: 巧妙的把戏也可能略微不老实。

intro.en: The adjective takes two inflections and grows an adverb and a noun.
intro.cn: 这个形容词有两种屈折形式，并长出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base: clever appears in Middle English with an uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语词基：clever 见于中古英语，来源不明。

She is the cleverest in the class.

items.meaning: a smart but possibly unfair act
items.meaningCN: 巧妙但可能不老实的做法
items.example: It was a clever trick with the cards.
items.exampleCN: 那是玩牌时的一个巧妙把戏。
